name: Neervannar Perumal Temple, Thiruneermalai
deity: Vishnu as Neervannar Perumal, with the Goddess Animamalar Mangai Thayar — and, on the hilltop, Ranganatha, Shanta Narasimha and Ulagalanda Perumal
period: A Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu, sung by Thirumangai Alvar and Bhoothathalvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: On a rocky hill south-west of Chennai, Vishnu is worshipped in four postures — standing, reclining, seated and striding — at Thiruneermalai, the Divya Desam of the 'holy water-hill'.

sections.history: Thiruneermalai, on the south-western edge of Chennai near Pallavaram, is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Thondai Nadu. Thirumangai Alvar and Bhoothathalvar sang of the Lord here, which places the shrine within the age of the early Alvar hymns. The place is really two temples in one sacred hill: a shrine at the foot, where Neervannar Perumal stands with Animamalar Mangai Thayar, and a second temple on the summit. Pilgrims have long climbed between the two, taking in the Lord in each of his postures.
sections.architecture: Two temples share the rock. At the foot of the hill stand Neervannar Perumal, the shrines of Kalyana Rama and of Andal. A long flight of steps leads to the hilltop temple, where Ranganatha reclines beneath the Ranga Vimana with Ranganayaki Thayar, Shanta Narasimha is seated, and Ulagalanda Perumal strides forward as Trivikrama. The hilltop shrine faces east. Four sacred tanks are named — Kshira, Karunya, Svarna and Siddha Pushkarini.
sections.legends: The name Thiruneermalai means the hill of holy water. Tradition tells that Thirumangai Alvar came here to worship, but the hill was ringed by floodwater and he could not cross. He waited for months until the waters drew back, and only then received the vision of the Lord on the hill. The place thus remembers a devotee's patience, and the Lord who is dark as water, Neervannar, waits at its foot.
sections.festivals: Vaikunta Ekadashi is observed here, and the temple keeps an annual Brahmotsavam with processions of the Lord from the foot of the hill. The days of the Alvars are honoured in the customary Vaishnava manner. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Few Divya Desams offer four postures of Vishnu in a single visit. Begin at the foot of the hill, then make the long climb to the summit, where the three forms of the hilltop temple wait; wear comfortable footwear for the steps. The climb is rewarded with a wide view over the surrounding country.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days and Vaikunta Ekadashi are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: At Thiruneermalai on the south-western edge of Chennai, near Pallavaram in Chengalpattu district; reached by road from Pallavaram and Tambaram. Chennai International Airport at Meenambakkam is close by.
